program: Older adult home modification and housing stability

what: North West Housing Partnership helps suburban Chicago residents repair homes and navigate housing decisions.
Its older adult home modification combines occupational therapy, nursing and contractor support.
Public partners help older and disabled residents remain safely at home.
strengths: Accessibility barriers are concrete and actionable.
Current public programs establish local delivery.
Repairs may protect independence and resources.
reservations: Annual additional cohorts and local clinical outcomes are unverified.
CAPABLE trials do not validate local QALYs or fidelity.
Public funding and property activity complicate donor returns.

sections.what: North West Housing Partnership, EIN 36-3715417, serves suburban Cook County and nearby Chicago metropolitan communities through housing development, rehabilitation and counseling. Current older adult home modification is HUD-funded and free, with occupational therapist, nurse and contractor input. The official support page solicits donations; checkout was not tested.
sections.monitoring: Municipal, IHDA, HUD and AgeOptions support remain in the counterfactual. No observed annual cohort is asserted. Track unique additional completed households, delivered visits, modifications, function, disruption and actual otherwise-paid spending. Forgivable loan principal, retail repair value and property appreciation are not household consumption gains.
sections.qualitative: The 2019 Baltimore CAPABLE trial found reduced ADL disability at five months after up to ten visits. A 2025 randomized trial after hospitalization found no statistically or clinically significant overall ADL improvement, although mobility improved. Neither establishes NWHP QALYs or net resources. The .03 utility increment for five months is a weak judgment, not an ADL-to-QALY conversion or validated local fidelity. No mortality, duplicate fall benefit or ordinary survivor earnings are priced.
sections.cost:
FY2025 original expense is $642,680; FY2024 is $542,871. FY2023 $902,809 expense plus $729,996 separately netted inventory cost gives $1,632,805 full recognized cost. Schedule D's $390,852 reconciliation is already included, not added twice. FY2024 minus $1 donated-service reconciliation is immaterial, not meaningful negative resources. FY2023 rental gross and net match in retrieved fields; absence of an addback is not proof of zero resources. Three-year mean is $939,452; property activity makes it imperfect operating comparison. Unrecognized volunteer and outside resources remain unknown.

Judged 100 local household opportunities and .5 additional annual-work response expose 50 households. Completion .6 yields 30 clinical residents within that union. Judged .03 utility for five months, quarter-year delay and 3% discount give .372239 clinical QALYs. Whole annual cost remains; this is a narrow conditional channel, not full portfolio or measured marginal-gift productivity.

Fifteen households conditionally avoid $1,000 actual repair spending and $500 net energy/care burdens in one year, net of taxes, benefits, replacement support and maintenance. Each positive component retains .5 for health overlap; negative components remain full. Full $100 disruption/time cost leaves $650. Thirty-five others lose $100. At $25,000 annual resources and one welfareperson per household, one joint log yields .121467 equivalents. Additional family welfare is unpriced. Combined .493706 gives $13.017467 million per ten combined equivalents, not ten clinical QALYs.

Resource exposure and costs survive clinical failure. Full 50-household harm and distinct local payer/contractor losses are stresses. Central outside incidence and harms are unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete-world benefit. Public and nonlocal opportunity costs remain unpriced.
sections.funding: FY2025 government grants are $122,697; prior years $394,031 and $145,526. Existing funded repairs, loans, owner spending and alternative providers continue. Response .5 is a judged additional annual funded-work fraction with full annual cost, not a second haircut on observed incremental output. b=1 is a sensitivity. Marginal gift expansion and funding replacement remain unknown.

model.geographicAttribution: Chicago metro households; clinical residents are a subset of resource exposure.
model.formula: exposed=N*b; clinical=exposed*completion; Q=clinical*q*discounted finite years−full union harm. Signed resource components preserve negatives, then one joint household log. Price=10*C/(health+resources).
model.counterfactual: Existing public repairs, loans, alternative providers and owner spending continue.
model.attribution: Throughput, additional annual response, completion, utility and actual spending are separate judgments.
model.uncertainty: Local outcomes, fidelity, outside incidence and marginal funding unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional completed home modifications, finite functional-health area and signed net household resources.
